source_text: Proceedings highlighted medical risks such as hemorrhage and infection, with speakers arguing that routine infant circumcision lacked sufficient evidence of net benefit, though mainstream pediatric bodies at the time, like the American Academy of Pediatrics, viewed it as culturally accepted with minimal risks outweighing rare complications.
